history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists the town as 'Balangir', but the temple stands at Harishankar village (Khaprakhol area), ~81 km from Balangir town, on the southern slopes of the Gandhamardan hills. The deity of Harisankar — 'Hari' (Vishnu) and 'Shankar' (Shiva) worshipped as one image, a rare symbol of Vaishnava–Shaiva harmony — was discovered by a Chauhan king of the Patna kingdom in the 14th century; the temple was constructed by order of Queen Durlabha Devi of Maharaja Vaijjal Dev Chauhan. A dancing Ganesha image traced to the early 12th century suggests earlier worship at the site, and one travel guide reports a stone inscription of 1246 CE (unverified). A stream flows past on a granite bed; the Nrusinghanath temple stands on the opposite slope, and the plateau between the two holds ancient Buddhist ruins identified as remnants of Parimalgiri University. town_description: Harishankar is a village in the Khaprakhol area of Balangir district, on the southern slopes of the Gandhamardan hills. The surrounding forests, waterfalls and holy springs make it a combined pilgrimage and nature destination.
